timing.summary: The explicit 16-byte salt obligation is required after the change and unsatisfied by the fixed old harness. Before the change, parser hashing used a key with its first word fixed to zero, so that same obligation was not applicable.

claims.necessity_reason: The retained coverage obligation concerns explicit selection of all 16 salt bytes for parsers this target creates and parses.

before.requirement: Explicitly select a 16-byte hash salt with a nonzero first key word before parsing.
before.reason: Before the change, the parser stored an unsigned-long salt and copied it into a SipHash key whose first word was fixed to zero. The reconstructed source also confirms no XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes definition in xmlparse.c.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows the available legacy setter accepted only an unsigned-long salt.
Confirms absence of the new setter definition in the reconstructed prior xmlparse.c.

after.requirement: Explicitly select a 16-byte hash salt with a nonzero first key word before parsing.
after.reason: The new public setter accepts 16 entropy bytes before parsing, and hashing copies the full stored key. The fixed harness still calls only the legacy setter, which zeros the first key word.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows the legacy setter's narrower effect.
Shows hashing receives the full stored key.

claims.comparison_reason: The same explicit 16-byte selection capability was unavailable in the before contract and is supported after the change. The old harness has no route to it.
